headline: High risk of filesystem conflict and cascading misuse: OpenHands can write broadly while marketingskills also writes files and shares context, creating unsafe default interaction pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: marketingskills explicitly says its tool-use pattern is that skills “reference each other and build on shared context,” while OpenHands can use MCP, browsers, and files in the runtime. That creates a plausible path where A’s generated content is consumed by B as trusted context. No direct raw-web parsing is documented, so medium is the higher justified severity.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs instruction-like text into a shared file or MCP-fed context that agent_b reads
IF agent_b treats shared skill/context files as authoritative without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared-context file handoff between the agents
Require provenance tags on any A-produced content before B reads it
Insert a manual review step before B executes instructions from A
Restrict B’s MCP servers to allowlisted, read-only endpoints
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read and write files, and OpenHands explicitly operates on files mounted into its runtime while marketingskills references shared context files. If sensitive marketing content lands in a shared workspace, either agent can expose it through its outputs or network egress. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default-style file workflows, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted to the same workspace or volume
IF marketing content or product marketing context includes confidential material
IF agent_b sends file contents to its configured model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces
Remove secrets from any shared mounted files
Turn off B’s broad network egress for sensitive runs
Use read-only mounts for A’s reference files
requires-engineering: add per-file data-class filtering

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A and B both have filesystem write, subprocess spawning, and multiple-instance support; B also modifies git state and can install packages. In a shared directory or mounted volume, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and corrupt state. Because B’s defaults are broad and A also writes files, the conflict is dangerous by default in shared setups.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share the same writable directory or mounted volume
IF agent_b performs git operations while agent_a is writing files
IF multiple instances of either agent run concurrently on the same repo
mitigations: Give each agent a separate working directory
Serialize git and filesystem writes with a lock
Run B in a disposable branch or clone
Make A’s output directory read-only to B
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: marketingskills is designed around shared context, so A’s outputs can become B’s inputs. OpenHands can act on files, shell, browser, and MCP tools, meaning B may operationalize A’s content without a built-in verification step. That is a classic cascading-error pathway, but not clearly irreversible by default, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated plans, facts, or code without independent verification
IF A’s shared-context output is used to trigger shell, browser, or MCP actions in B
mitigations: Require B to verify A’s claims against primary sources
Add a checklist that blocks action until human approval
Limit A to drafting only, not authoritative instructions
Log and diff A-to-B handoffs for review
requires-engineering: implement confidence/provenance gating

E_compliance.rationale: A touches marketing content and product marketing context, while B handles files in a runtime and may send data to a user-configured model provider. The profiles do not show a specific residency or regulated-data mismatch, so only a low compliance concern is supported. I do not cite only one agent because the risk arises from their combined handling and transmission path.
conditions: IF regulated or customer-identifying marketing data is placed into the shared runtime
IF B’s configured model provider is outside the required residency or contractual boundary
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared runtime
Use a provider with the required residency and DPA
Redact customer identifiers before handoff
Review retention settings for the model provider
requires-engineering: enforce residency-aware routing
